title: Future: I will write, I'm going to write

blocks.text: The imperfective verb has 3 tenses: the present, the past, and the future. The perfective verb has 2 tenses: the past and the future.
**Future tense after «когда» and «как только».** In a sentence referring to the future with a subordinate clause introduced by "when" or "as soon as" the verbs of both clauses are in the future:

items: Я буду читать письма, когда ты будешь учить диалог.

blocks.text: An action of the subordinate clause which is to be completed before the action of the main clause is rendered by the perfective future:

items: Когда я сделаю уроки, я буду слушать радио.
Как только я получу от него письмо, я напишу вам.

blocks.text: The future condition is expressed in English by the present tense, whereas in Russian it is expressed by the future: *Я пойду в школу завтра, если я буду здоров.* — I'll go to school tomorrow if I am well.

items: We will ask at a travel agency.
I will not see him any more.
Now you will start to warm up.
No one will notice the substitution.

exercises.why: **стать → станешь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**сделать → сделаем** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**дать → дам** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**спросить → Спросим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
exercises.prompt: We will ask at a travel agency.

exercises.why: **взять → возьмешь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**пойти → пойду** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**выйти → выйду** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**увидеть → увижу** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
exercises.prompt: I will not see him any more.

exercises.why: **прийти → придёт** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
**начать → начнёшь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
exercises.prompt: Now you will start to warm up.

exercises.why: **заметить → заметит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
exercises.prompt: No one will notice the substitution.

exercises.why: **остаться → останется** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Я не ___ (быть) спать, Гортензио, пока не увижу её.
exercises.prompt: I will not sleep, Hortensio, till I see her.
exercises.why: **быть → буду** — future of быть: 1st person singular.

exercises.prompt: The current session settings will be used.
exercises.why: **быть → Будут** — future of быть: 3rd person plural.

exercises.q: Шестидесятичетырёхразрядное программное обеспечение не ___ (быть) работать на тридцатидвухразрядной архитектуре.
exercises.prompt: Sixty-four-bit software will not run on 32-bit architecture.
exercises.why: **быть → будет** — future of быть: 3rd person singular.
